event.title: Severe Flooding in Japan Due to Record Rainfall Causes Deaths and Disruptions
event.canonical_title: Severe Flooding in Japan Due to Record Rainfall Causes Deaths and Disruptions
event.summary: Unprecedented rainfall in Japan's Chiba prefecture has resulted in at least four fatalities and left approximately 7,000 passengers stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport. Authorities issued the highest-level rain warning for the first time, prompting evacuation orders for around 400,000 residents due to flooding risks and landslide alerts. Power outages affected over 20,000 households as the torrential rains continued to impact the region.

event_overview.title: About Japan Flooding
event_overview.subject: Japan Flooding
event_overview.summary: Japan Flooding refers to the heavy-rain emergency that began affecting eastern Japan on August 13, 2026, with the most severe reported impacts centered on Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo. Intense short-duration rainfall flooded roads and homes, disrupted transport and power service, and prompted warnings for both inundation and landslides; casualty figures remained subject to official confirmation as response operations continued.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The event was reported as beginning on August 13, 2026; the selected timeline follows developments reported through August 15, 2026, rather than establishing a final end date.

facts.label: Primary area affected
facts.value: The acute flooding emergency was concentrated in Chiba Prefecture in eastern Japan, near Tokyo, although the broader weather system affected eastern Japan.

facts.label: Meteorological hazard
facts.value: The rainfall was characterized as record-breaking in parts of Chiba, with forecasts and reports of more than 100 millimeters of rain in an hour in Chiba City and nearby municipalities; the associated risks included urban flooding and landslides.

facts.label: Warnings and public-warning system
facts.value: The Japan Meteorological Agency issued its highest-level heavy-rain warning for 14 Chiba municipalities during the event. In Chiba, JMA weather warnings and advisories have been issued on a municipality-by-municipality basis since 2010.

facts.label: Reported human impact
facts.value: By August 14, reporting cited at least five deaths in Chiba after the rainfall and flooding. This was an early reported toll and may be revised as authorities verify cases.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate August 14-15, 2026 flooding and fatality reports, not a complete accounting of all weather impacts, response measures, damage assessments, or later revisions to casualties.
